metadata.title: Seed Domain: Language Binding
metadata.description: Machine-parseable seed graph for binding words, gestures, symbols, sentences, questions, stories, tone, and context to relation clusters.
notes: This graph uses the 179 first-set language-binding situations, not all 254 high-priority rows.
Language is represented as surface forms attached to relation clusters, not as the first source of meaning.
The seed is intentionally compact and excludes a full grammar ontology or dictionary.

layers.label: Language Observation Channels
layers.description: Observable channels for speech, gesture, writing, prosody, context, social interaction, and story sequence.

layers.label: Language Relational Invariants
layers.description: Reusable reference, context, role, property, quantity, spatial, temporal, causal, polarity, and discourse relations.

layers.label: Language Binding Schemas
layers.description: Reusable mechanisms for binding surface forms to relation clusters and sentence structures.

layers.label: Surface Forms
layers.description: Spoken, gestural, written, tonal, and language-variant surfaces.

layers.label: Participants
layers.description: Speaker, listener, referent, and shared-attention participant handles.

layers.label: Referents And Events
layers.description: Objects, properties, sets, actions, stories, promises, and contexts that language can refer to.

layers.label: Language Abstractions
layers.description: Higher-level abstractions created by relation-cluster binding, contextual meaning, symbolic reference, and story understanding.

nodes.label: speech sound observation
nodes.summary: Source for spoken words, syllables, phoneme contrasts, and partial pronunciations.

nodes.label: gesture observation
nodes.summary: Source for pointing, waving, nodding, shaking head, blocking, and permission gestures.

nodes.label: written mark observation
nodes.summary: Source for signs, letters, written words, numerals, and public symbols.

nodes.label: prosody and tone observation
nodes.summary: Source for happy, angry, joking, serious, gentle, and sharp tone differences.

nodes.label: context observation
nodes.summary: Source for selecting which relation cluster a surface form should activate.

nodes.label: social interaction observation
nodes.summary: Source for speaker, listener, permission, promise, question, and answer structure.

nodes.label: story sequence observation
nodes.summary: Source for ordered story events, retelling, prediction, problem, and solution.

nodes.label: reference
nodes.summary: Links a surface form to a referent, action, property, event, or relation cluster.

nodes.label: context selection
nodes.summary: Selects which relation subset should be active for a surface form.

nodes.label: surface/meaning separation
nodes.summary: Separates word shape or sound from the relation cluster it can activate.

nodes.label: same/different
nodes.summary: Compares whether forms, objects, labels, or meanings match or differ.

nodes.label: agent role
nodes.summary: Tracks speaker, listener, giver, receiver, doer, undergoer, owner, and referent roles.

nodes.label: property relation
nodes.summary: Tracks color, size, shape, weight, state, and selected attributes.

nodes.label: quantity relation
nodes.summary: Tracks counts, sets, all, none, some, more, less, and comparison.

nodes.label: spatial relation
nodes.summary: Tracks here, there, inside, outside, on, under, and location relations.

nodes.label: temporal order
nodes.summary: Tracks before, after, when, past, present, future, and event order.

nodes.label: action/effect
nodes.summary: Tracks action words, event transitions, and result states.

nodes.label: permission/blocking
nodes.summary: Tracks allowed, blocked, prohibited, delayed, and conditionally permitted actions.

nodes.label: cause/effect
nodes.summary: Tracks because links, event causes, and explanatory connections.

nodes.label: condition/rule
nodes.summary: Tracks if, when, and conditionally selected action or permission.

nodes.label: negation/polarity
nodes.summary: Tracks not, nothing, absence, non-event, and prohibited action.

nodes.label: uncertainty strength
nodes.summary: Tracks think, know, maybe, believe, want, and expected.

nodes.label: sequence/discourse
nodes.summary: Tracks story order, explanation, problem, solution, promise, and prediction.

nodes.label: sound-form contrast
nodes.summary: Tracks phoneme contrast, syllable structure, mispronunciation, and approximate word recognition.

nodes.label: word handle
nodes.summary: A surface word acts as a handle into a relation cluster.

nodes.label: relation cluster binding
nodes.summary: A meaning is represented as strong and weak relations activated together.

nodes.label: contextual relation activation
nodes.summary: Context selects the relevant subset of a relation cluster.

nodes.label: name binding
nodes.summary: A name or role word refers to an agent or familiar social handle.

nodes.label: social role word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as mama and papa bind to familiar social roles.

nodes.label: gesture-word pairing
nodes.summary: A gesture and spoken form support the same permission, direction, or social signal.

nodes.label: permission word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as yes and okay mark allowed action.

nodes.label: prohibition word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as no and stop mark blocked or unsafe action.

nodes.label: delay word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as wait mark delayed access or delayed action.

nodes.label: object label binding
nodes.summary: An object word labels an object instance or category cluster.

nodes.label: category extension
nodes.summary: The same word extends across object sizes, colors, pictures, and instances.

nodes.label: picture-object reference
nodes.summary: A picture can stand for an object or category.

nodes.label: property label binding
nodes.summary: A property word labels color, size, shape, temperature, texture, weight, or state.

nodes.label: modifier-property binding
nodes.summary: A modifier selects a property dimension of an object or event.

nodes.label: predicate property sentence
nodes.summary: A sentence assigns a property or state to a subject.

nodes.label: quantity word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as more, less, all, none, and some bind to quantity relations.

nodes.label: count word binding
nodes.summary: Number words bind to distinct item counts and counting correspondence.

nodes.label: set quantifier binding
nodes.summary: Every, some, only, all, and none select set scope.

nodes.label: comparison question binding
nodes.summary: Questions such as how many and which is bigger query quantity or comparison slots.

nodes.label: logical connector binding
nodes.summary: And, or, either, and both bind to filters over relation sets.

nodes.label: spatial word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as here, there, inside, outside, on, and under bind to spatial relations.

nodes.label: temporal word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as before, after, and when bind to event order.

nodes.label: state word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as open, closed, empty, gone, hot, and wet bind to state relations.

nodes.label: ordered instruction binding
nodes.summary: Instruction language orders action steps.

nodes.label: action word binding
nodes.summary: A verb binds to an action relation.

nodes.label: event transition binding
nodes.summary: Words such as fall, break, and spill bind to state-changing events.

nodes.label: result state binding
nodes.summary: Language connects an event to the resulting state.

nodes.label: social action word binding
nodes.summary: Words such as give, take, share, help, and hurt bind to social action relations.

nodes.label: speaker-addressee binding
nodes.summary: I and you resolve by speaker and listener position.

nodes.label: pronoun perspective binding
nodes.summary: Pronoun meaning changes with speaker, listener, and referent.

nodes.label: possessive relation binding
nodes.summary: Mine and yours bind to ownership or possession from a perspective.

nodes.label: transfer role binding
nodes.summary: Gave and took mark giver, receiver, source, and object roles.

nodes.label: sentence-event binding
nodes.summary: A sentence binds words and order to an event relation.

nodes.label: agent-patient role binding
nodes.summary: Word order marks who acted and who was acted on.

nodes.label: preposition phrase binding
nodes.summary: A preposition phrase attaches location or relation to an entity or event.

nodes.label: modifier scope binding
nodes.summary: Modifier position selects which entity or event gets the property.

nodes.label: relative clause binding
nodes.summary: A relative clause constrains or describes a referent.

nodes.label: attachment ambiguity binding
nodes.summary: Context resolves whether a phrase modifies one relation or another.

nodes.label: question relation query
nodes.summary: A question asks for a missing relation slot such as who, where, what, why, or how many.

nodes.label: answer slot binding
nodes.summary: An answer fills the relation slot requested by a question.

nodes.label: word correction repair
nodes.summary: A wrong word is corrected and the relation cluster is adjusted.

nodes.label: partial utterance resolution
nodes.summary: Context resolves a partial child utterance into a likely word handle.

nodes.label: unfamiliar word negotiation
nodes.summary: A speaker asks what a word means and seeks its relation cluster.

nodes.label: public sign binding
nodes.summary: A public sign links a written or visual symbol to an action rule.

nodes.label: written symbol binding
nodes.summary: Written marks bind to word, quantity, or action relation clusters.

nodes.label: symbol-to-action binding
nodes.summary: A symbol such as stop activates a behavior rule.

nodes.label: symbol-to-quantity binding
nodes.summary: A written numeral binds to a quantity relation.

nodes.label: story event chain
nodes.summary: A story is a sequence of relation events.

nodes.label: narrative order binding
nodes.summary: Beginning, middle, and end bind to story order.

nodes.label: promise language binding
nodes.summary: Promise language creates an expected future action.

nodes.label: rule story binding
nodes.summary: Story language can represent rule following or violation.

nodes.label: problem-solution discourse
nodes.summary: A story can contain a problem state and a solution state.

nodes.label: prediction from story state
nodes.summary: Current story state supports prediction of what may happen next.

nodes.label: conditional clause binding
nodes.summary: An if clause sets a condition for action or outcome.

nodes.label: causal clause binding
nodes.summary: A because clause links a cause to an effect.

nodes.label: prohibition clause binding
nodes.summary: A do-not clause blocks an action relation.

nodes.label: and/or filter binding
nodes.summary: And and or select required or alternative relation filters.

nodes.label: when trigger binding
nodes.summary: A when clause marks an event trigger.

nodes.label: polysemy context selection
nodes.summary: The same surface word selects different relation clusters in different contexts.

nodes.label: word sense split
nodes.summary: A word form can split into separate sense clusters.

nodes.label: pragmatic force binding
nodes.summary: A sentence form can act as question, command, joke, serious statement, or request.

nodes.label: indirect request binding
nodes.summary: An apparent ability question can function as a request.

nodes.label: prosody-affect binding
nodes.summary: Tone changes affective prediction while the word form stays the same.

nodes.label: cross-language label equivalence
nodes.summary: Two language forms can point to the same relation cluster.

nodes.label: phoneme contrast binding
nodes.summary: A small sound difference can change the word candidate.

nodes.label: syllable structure binding
nodes.summary: A word can be segmented into syllables or smaller sound units.

nodes.label: approximate word recognition
nodes.summary: A partial or mispronounced form can still activate a likely relation cluster through context.

nodes.label: negation operator binding
nodes.summary: Not negates a property, location, action, or event relation.

nodes.label: absence word binding
nodes.summary: Nothing, none, and gone bind to absence relations.

nodes.label: tense event time binding
nodes.summary: Tense words and verb forms mark event time.

nodes.label: epistemic strength binding
nodes.summary: Think, know, maybe, and believe mark confidence or belief strength.

nodes.label: desire belief expectation binding
nodes.summary: Want, believe, and expected bind to internal-state and future-expectation relations.

nodes.label: spoken word
nodes.summary: A spoken word form.

nodes.label: gesture
nodes.summary: A visible gesture form paired with speech or action.

nodes.label: written mark
nodes.summary: A written or printed mark.

nodes.label: tone
nodes.summary: The affective or pragmatic tone over speech.

nodes.label: home-language word
nodes.summary: A word form from the child's home language.

nodes.label: speaker
nodes.summary: The person producing the utterance.

nodes.label: listener
nodes.summary: The person receiving or interpreting the utterance.

nodes.label: referent person
nodes.summary: A person referred to by a name, role, pronoun, or description.

nodes.label: shared attention partner
nodes.summary: A partner attending to the same object or event.

nodes.label: object referent
nodes.summary: An object named, described, located, moved, or acted on.

nodes.label: picture referent
nodes.summary: A picture that stands for an object or category.

nodes.label: property referent
nodes.summary: A property such as red, soft, round, hot, wet, empty, or heavy.

nodes.label: quantity set referent
nodes.summary: A set or count described by all, none, some, one, two, every, or only.

nodes.label: location referent
nodes.summary: A location relation such as here, there, inside, outside, on, or under.

nodes.label: action event referent
nodes.summary: An action or event such as push, fall, break, spill, eat, give, or take.

nodes.label: sentence referent
nodes.summary: A sentence that binds words into an event or relation.

nodes.label: question referent
nodes.summary: A question form that asks for a missing relation slot.

nodes.label: story event referent
nodes.summary: A story event or chain of events.

nodes.label: promise outcome referent
nodes.summary: A promise and its later fulfilled or violated outcome.

nodes.label: context referent
nodes.summary: The situation that selects meaning.

nodes.label: meaning as relation cluster
nodes.summary: A meaning is a relation cluster with strong and weak links.

nodes.label: language binding
nodes.summary: Surface forms bind to relation structures learned elsewhere.

nodes.label: contextual meaning
nodes.summary: Context changes which relation cluster is selected.

nodes.label: symbolic reference
nodes.summary: A mark, sign, word, or picture can stand for another relation structure.

nodes.label: story understanding
nodes.summary: Story comprehension is ordered relation-chain understanding.

micro_experiences.title: Name, gesture, yes, no, stop, and wait
events: caregiver says the child's name
caregiver says no while blocking
caregiver nods yes
caregiver says wait while delaying access
language_overlay: A word, a gesture, and the allowed or blocked action are bound together.

micro_experiences.title: Object labels generalize across instances
events: caregiver says ball while touching one ball
caregiver says ball for a different sized ball
caregiver says ball for a picture
language_overlay: Ball is not one object; it is a handle into a category relation cluster.

micro_experiences.title: Property and quantity words modify referents
events: caregiver says red block
caregiver says more food
caregiver asks how many biscuits
caregiver says every child got a sweet
language_overlay: Property and quantity words select relation dimensions rather than naming whole objects.

micro_experiences.title: Spatial and temporal words guide action
events: caregiver says put the ball in the box
caregiver says take it out
caregiver says wash hands before eating
language_overlay: Inside, outside, before, and after bind speech to spatial and ordered-action relations.

micro_experiences.title: Verb words bind to action-effect structure
events: caregiver says push while pushing
caregiver says fall after a toy falls
caregiver says spill after water leaves the cup
language_overlay: A verb points to an action and its expected event transition or result state.

micro_experiences.title: Pronouns and transfer roles depend on perspective
events: speaker says I
speaker says you
caregiver says the child gave the toy to the sibling
caregiver says the sibling took the toy
language_overlay: I and you change with speaker; gave and took change giver, receiver, and object roles.

micro_experiences.title: Sentence order changes event roles
events: caregiver says the child chased the dog
caregiver says the dog chased the child
caregiver says the ball hit the cup
caregiver says the cup hit the ball
language_overlay: The same words can create different events when grammar roles reverse.

micro_experiences.title: Questions ask for missing relation slots
events: caregiver asks where is the ball
caregiver asks why the floor is wet
child says a wrong word and adult corrects it
language_overlay: Where asks for location, why asks for cause, and correction updates the word-relation link.

micro_experiences.title: Signs and written marks bind to action and quantity
events: child sees a stop sign
adult says stop
child sees number 3 beside three dots
language_overlay: Written symbols are public handles into action or quantity relations.

micro_experiences.title: Stories bind promises, rules, problems, and solutions
events: story character promises to return
character breaks the promise
story shows a rule followed
child predicts what happens next
language_overlay: A story is an ordered relation chain, not a bag of sentences.

micro_experiences.title: If, because, and not modify relation structures
events: caregiver says if the light is red, stop
caregiver says the cup fell because it was near the edge
caregiver says the cup is not red
language_overlay: Logical words modify existing relation structures instead of becoming isolated facts.

micro_experiences.title: Context, tone, and sound shape word interpretation
events: light means easy to lift in one context
light means illumination in another
same word is happy or angry by tone
child says ba for ball and context resolves it
language_overlay: Surface form, tone, context, and relation cluster must be represented separately.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is a word not the same thing as its meaning?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A word is a surface handle that activates a relation cluster. Context decides which strong and weak relations become active.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can ball apply to balls of different sizes and colors?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The word activates an object-label cluster that extends across instances while preserving category-relevant relations.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is red ball different from ball?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Red is a property modifier that selects a property relation on the object-label cluster.

evaluation_questions.question: Why are the dog chased the child and the child chased the dog different?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The same words are assigned different agent and patient roles by sentence structure.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation slot does where is the ball ask for?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Where asks for the missing spatial/location slot of the object relation cluster.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can light mean easy to lift or illumination?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The same surface word is routed through context selection to different relation clusters.

evaluation_questions.question: How does not change the cup is red?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Negation modifies the property assertion while keeping the same target relation structure in view.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does a broken promise change later expectation?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Promise language creates a predicted future action; when the outcome violates it, story state and reliability expectation change.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can ba be understood as ball when the child points to a ball?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Approximate sound recognition and context jointly select the likely word handle and relation cluster.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can can you open the door function as a request?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Pragmatic force and context convert an ability question into an indirect request for action.
